narrative.overview:
The game is a table shared by two people. Every screen is the same object seen from above: a vermilion cloth half and an indigo cloth half, meeting at a seam, with a warm paper garden board lying across that seam. The half whose turn it is lights up; the waiting half sinks to a darker, muted dye. Nothing floats on a neutral page. A thin top bar carries only the match label and two icon buttons; everything about a player (their name, tokens in hand, the tile they must answer, the result) sits in their own half of the cloth.

The world is made of a few real materials. The dyes and the paper carry raster texture (a plain-weave cloth tile and a fibre paper tile, both 256px seamless tiles, soft-light blended onto flat colour). Tokens are lacquered discs with a radial sheen. The garden's sixteen tiles are the client's own SVG art, kept as drawn; the system frames them and never redraws them. Paper surfaces (the order card, the sheets) are the only places interface text sits on light; everything else is cream type on dye.

The interface recedes. The garden is the largest thing on every screen at every viewport, and every other element is sized from what is left over. Motion belongs to the play itself: the light crossing the seam, a taken tile flying to the mover's card, a token settling into its cell, a brush stroke through a winning formation.
keyCharacteristics: Two dyed halves (vermilion, indigo), stacked in portrait and side by side in landscape, meeting at the garden's centre.
One paper garden on the seam, as large as the viewport allows (up to 640px portrait, 760px landscape).
Lit versus sunk dye is the turn indicator; players are also told apart by token pattern (crest versus plain).
Cream type on cloth, ink type on paper; controls invert their colours when they land on paper.
A serif display face for names, results and titles only; a humanist sans for everything else.
Real texture, soft-light blended; authored SVG icons, tokens and diagrams.

rules.name: The Lit Half Rule
rules.body: Exactly one half is lit: the half of the player to move. The other sits in its sunk dye. A tie lights both at half strength. No other element may claim the lit dye.

rules.name: The One Action Colour Rule
rules.body: On paper, vermilion is the only action colour. On the dyes, the primary action is a paper button. Indigo is a player, never a button.

rules.name: The Gold Marks Rule
rules.body: Gold is for what the game marks (may be taken, last placed, won, scored) and for focus on the dyes. It is never a fill for interface chrome.

rules.name: The Eighteen Pixel Rule
rules.body: The display face is set at 18px or above only; below that everything is Source Sans 3. The smallest live display use (a seat name on a short phone) computes to about 19px.

rules.name: The Seat Scale Rule
rules.body: Everything in a seat is sized in em from one seat font size (1rem default; 0.9375rem and 0.875rem on short screens; clamp(0.875rem, 0.25rem + 1.2vw, 1.5rem) in landscape), so a seat scales as a whole.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Token counts and points use tabular figures.

rules.name: The Garden First Rule
rules.body: The garden is sized first and is the largest element at every viewport; seats, bars and cards fit around it, and short screens drop secondary detail before the garden shrinks further.

rules.name: The Shade Layer Rule
rules.body: Tiles that may not be taken sink under a warm shade layer (rgba(70,54,36,.3), .38 once the game is over) drawn as a pseudo-element, never a CSS filter: filters on these SVG-filled buttons crashed WebKit during play.

rules.name: The Texture Rule
rules.body: Cloth and paper texture is a 256px seamless tile in grey light and shade, soft-light blended over flat colour. A new surface of cloth or paper uses the same tiles the same way; texture is never a photograph or a gradient imitation.

dos: **Do** split every screen into the vermilion and indigo halves with the paper garden on the seam, stacked in portrait, side by side from aspect 5/4.
**Do** light only the half of the player to move, with the lit dye and a radial light brightest at the seam, animating opacity alone.
**Do** put cream type on the dyes and ink type on paper, and swap a control's material when it moves from cloth to paper.
**Do** size the garden first and let short screens drop pips and notes before the garden shrinks.
**Do** keep every touch target at least 44px.
**Do** blend the cloth and paper texture tiles (256px, soft-light) under any new cloth or paper surface.
**Do** draw new icons as SVG on the 24px grid with a 1.8 stroke, round caps and joins, in currentColor.
**Do** keep the display face to 18px and above and set everything smaller in Source Sans 3.
donts: **Don't** redraw, restyle or recolour the garden tile art; frame it only. The rising sun stays a plain disc.
**Don't** tell players apart by colour alone: player 1's tokens carry the five-petal crest, player 2's stay plain.
**Don't** put the board on a neutral page or move player information into a status bar or side panel; it lives in that player's half.
**Don't** use indigo as an action colour or gold as a fill for interface chrome.
**Don't** apply CSS filters to garden cells; shade them with a layer.
**Don't** add a motion that has no reduced-motion fallback to an instant state change.
